html:
SMTO-POL-0015 — An admin command can't run inside a group of commands

GUID: f07af924-635f-4f84-855b-2478f0670feb
Slug: sequence-privilege-unsupported
Domain: POL · Subsystem: pol

What happened

  • The Agent put a command that needs administrator rights (sudo) inside a group of commands. SMTO only runs such commands one at a time with their own approval, so the group was stopped before its commands ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reply in the conversation asking the Agent to run the command that needs administrator rights by itself, not inside a group of commands. Commands that need administrator rights are accepted only as single commands, each checked on its own.
  2. If an Approval needed card appears for that single command, read it and select Approve once only if it's what you want. Your approval then covers just that one command, not the others in the group.
  3. Let the Agent run the remaining ordinary commands afterwards. Commands that don't need administrator rights can still run together as a group.

What success looks like

  • The admin command runs as a single step, and the other commands run after it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask the Agent to run the whole group with administrator rights; that would give extra power to commands that don't need it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A shell__sequence child normalized to managed sudo, and the sequence carries no unsafe grant for privileged children, so the sequence was rejected with sequence_privilege_unsupported before its steps ran.

What this means

  • Managed sudo normalization in a sequence requires authority that an ordinary sequence does not carry for each privileged child. Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Managed sudo normalization in a sequence requires authority that an ordinary sequence does not carry for each privileged child.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the normalized privileged child and active Gate sudo mode; compare its exact command with the supported ordinary shell approval flow.

How to fix it

  • Run the privileged command through an ordinary shell__command call so managed sudo applies its own approval and unsafe grant (execution/sudo_handler.py sequence_rejection), and keep unprivileged steps in the sequence. Do not elevate the whole sequence or disable the managed-sudo gate.
  • Use the ordinary Shell command flow for the specific privileged operation and its explicit approval. Do not elevate unrelated sequence children or disable the privilege guard.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended privileged command passes its own supported shell authorization without elevating unrelated children.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Policy and approval decisions are scoped to their owning operation. Existing receipts determine prior effects; this explanation neither grants authority nor changes retry ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
